data.title: An argument for increasing TCP's initial congestion window (2024)
data.author: cyb0rg0
data.article_summary: 这篇文章建议再次提高TCP初始拥塞窗口值。作者回顾了2011年谷歌将TCP初始拥塞窗口从1-3提升到10（约15KB数据）的背景，指出这在当时能覆盖85%的网络资源请求。然而随着现代网页资源（如JS和图片）体积激增，大多数资源已达数百KB，现有窗口设置再次成为性能瓶颈。但作者也指出，若将窗口值直接提升一个数量级可能导致网络拥塞。因此需要在提升传输效率与避免网络拥塞之间寻求平衡。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TCP拥塞控制算法（如BBR、CUBIC）及其相关技术（如QUIC、L4S）的性能、适用性和潜在问题。

不同观点：
• **关于BBR和初始拥塞窗口（initcwnd）的争议**：
  - kev009认为BBR在初始阶段并不比其他拥塞控制算法优越，且提高initcwnd可能导致尾部丢包（tail loss），尤其在初始连接阶段。他还提到QUIC虽然简化了拥塞控制，但仍需面对类似TCP的权衡问题。
  - wahern反驳了QUIC完全消除拥塞窗口的观点，指出QUIC通常使用与TCP相同的拥塞控制算法（如CUBIC和BBR），但可能有更多调优自由度。

• **关于L4S技术的讨论**：
  - namibj提到L4S（低延迟、低丢失、可扩展吞吐量）技术可以通过更频繁的拥塞反馈（如每100个包反馈一次）减少丢包，从而优化拥塞控制。他引用了RFC 9330和RFC 9331中的数学关系（p_C ~= (p_L / k)^2）来说明L4S的优势。

• **关于TCP拥塞控制算法的历史与分类**：
  - egberts1强调Sally Floyd等人的研究对TCP拥塞控制算法的全面影响，并分类算法为反应式（基于丢包）、主动式（基于延迟）和预测式（基于带宽估计）。他还列举了多种TCP变体（如Vegas、CUBIC、BBR）及其研究文献。

补充讨论：
- **无线网络环境下的表现**：howtofly提问BBR在无线网络（高RTT波动）中的性能，但未得到直接回应。
- **DDOS攻击的潜在影响**：Hnrobert42质疑提高initcwnd是否会增加DDOS攻击的脆弱性，但未展开讨论。
- **缓冲膨胀（bufferbloat）的争议**：commandersaki认为缓冲膨胀问题在2010年代后已因网络改进而不再重要，但未提供具体证据。

争议焦点：
- BBR的实际效果与initcwnd的调优风险（kev009 vs. wahern）。
- QUIC是否真正摆脱了拥塞窗口的限制（wahern vs. 其他观点）。
- 缓冲膨胀问题的现实重要性（commandersaki vs. 未明确反对的观点）。

44889673.article_content:
An Argument for Increasing TCP's Initial Congestion Window ... Again
Published September 2, 2024
Introduction
Google has a long history of performing networking research, making changes, and pushing those changes to the entire internet. In 2011, they published
one of my favorite papers
, which described their decision to increase the TCP initial congestion window from 1 to 10 on their entire infrastructure. This was soon followed by an
RFC filed with the IETF
, and eventually became an internet standard.
I think it’s time to revisit that paper and update Google’s recommendations for the modern Internet.
TCP Initial Congestion Window
TCP uses an idea called the sliding window to manage how much data is in transit on the network at any given time. The receiver manages a receive window that tells the sender how much data it is willing to receive at once. In modern TCP, the receive window is set very high and only reduces if the receiver is running out of capacity. The goal is to ensure the receiver is never limiting the data transfer speed with a low window.
At the same time, the sender manages something called a congestion window. This value is the number of packets the sender can send at one time before it needs to pause and wait for a response from the receiver. There are various congestion control algorithms that adjust the congestion window, but the general goal of all of them is to ramp up transmission until it’s as fast as possible without being affected by congestion or packet loss somewhere in the network.
These congestion control algorithms require a seed value at the start of a transmission known as the initial congestion window. This value determines how much data can be sent at the beginning of a connection.
In traditional TCP (pre-2010), that value was set anywhere between 1 and 3, depending on OS and software. The predominant congestion control algorithm at that time, TCP New Reno, would increase the congestion window by an initial congestion window for every round trip with no packet loss. So a successful connection with no loss would look something like this:
Initial congestion window: 2. 2 packets sent (3 KB).
Congestion window: 4. 6 KB sent.
Congestion window: 6. 9 KB sent.
And so on…
If that connection runs into some packet loss, that congestion window is then cut in half and has to slowly recover. Eventually, in a long connection, the congestion window will settle in to a relatively narrow set of values, and this steady state condition is called convergence.
This scheme makes sense for the network traffic TCP was designed for. Large file transfers are minimally affected by this initial ramp up period. Depending on the round trip time of the connection, convergence can occur within 1 or 2 seconds, which isn’t too long for a file transfer that’s expected to take several minutes.
However, this convergence period has an adverse affect on the predominant communication on the internet: web page loads and API calls.
HTTP over TCP
Both web page loads and API calls use HTTP(s), and in the late 2000’s, they always used TCP as the transport layer.
A typical HTTP request looks like this on the network:
TCP connection is established
TLS encryption is established
Client sends an HTTP request (anywhere from 20 - 8000 bytes)
Server sends an HTTP response (anywhere from 100 bytes - 10 MB)
Crucially, the statistical distribution of both request and response sizes skews towards the higher end of those ranges. I’m certainly not the first person to say that the internet is bloated.
When TCP’s initial congestion window is set to something like 2, the largest request or response that can be sent in a single round trip is 3 KB. And in 2011, that was only about 40% of responses on the internet. That means 60% of assets that had to load for a web page to render had to wait at least an extra round trip to fully download. For typical internet round trips, that’s an extra 30ms for each of the 60+ assets that might be more than 3 KB. That means this web page will take an extra 1.2 seconds to load.
Google’s original recommendation
Because of that data, Google chose to increase the initial congestion window on their infrastructure to 10, a round trip data cutoff of 15 KB. Their calculations showed that this would allow nearly 85% of assets being served to users to load in a single round trip.
However, this doesn’t hold true on the 2020s internet. The use of both Javascript and images has skyrocketed, so the initial page loads on websites on modern websites consist of hundreds of assets, most of them 100s of KB in size. The increased bloat of the modern internet is causing us to run into the same problem again.
What Should We Do Now?
The challenge we face now is that just increasing the initial congestion window by another order of magnitude could be counterproductive. If web servers all over the internet start blasting out 100s of packets at a time, we will just be causing the congestion and packet loss that TCP tries to

data.title: PuTTY has a new website
data.author: GalaxySnail
data.article_summary: PuTTY是一款免费的SSH客户端软件，适用于Windows和Unix系统，包含xterm风格的终端模拟器。由Simon Tatham主要开发和维护。用户可直接访问下载页面获取最新版本或浏览主网站。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[PuTTY官方网站的设计和域名问题，以及其在用户中的情感价值和实际使用情况]

不同观点：
• **支持PuTTY现有网站设计**  
  - PuTTY团队明确表示不希望更换域名或网站设计，认为当前设计简单易用且易于通过搜索引擎找到。  
  - 用户认为其“原始”风格反而增加了可信度（“只有计算机科学家才会设计如此简陋的网站”）。  
  - 部分用户对网站有情感依恋，认为其具有怀旧价值（“几十年的记忆”）。  

• **批评PuTTY现有网站设计**  
  - 有人认为其过时的设计和复杂的URL导致信任问题，尤其是在下载二进制文件时难以辨别真伪。  
  - 批评者指出，Google搜索不再可靠，可能影响用户找到真正的官方网站。  

• **PuTTY的实际使用情况**  
  - 一些用户因Windows内置Terminal和OpenSSH而减少了对PuTTY的依赖，但仍用于嵌入式系统的串口通信。  
  - 有人提到PuTTY在某些严格的安全环境中是唯一可用的SSH工具。  

• **域名争议**  
  - 近期争议聚焦于第三方控制putty.org域名的问题，引发对开源项目域名被“劫持”的担忧。  
  - 用户指出PuTTY团队并未控制putty.org，而是由第三方运营，可能存在利益冲突。  

补充讨论：  
- 部分用户对PuTTY的功能提出改进建议，例如支持.pem密钥。  
- 有人提到PuTTY的CLI版本在Terminal中的使用体验较好。  
- Simon Tatham的其他作品（如游戏）也受到用户高度评价，甚至被视为其“免罪金牌”。

data.title: Good system design
data.author: dondraper36
data.article_summary:
这篇文章批判了当前社交媒体上流行的糟糕系统设计建议，并提出了作者认为的良好系统设计原则。主要内容包括：

1. 指出LinkedIn和Twitter上常见的两类误导性系统设计建议，认为它们对新手工程师有害无益。

2. 定义系统设计是"服务组装"的艺术，其基本构件包括应用服务器、数据库、缓存等。

3. 提出良好系统设计的特征：简单可靠、长期稳定运行而不引人注意，复杂系统往往意味着设计缺陷。

4. 强调状态管理是系统设计的核心难点，建议尽量减少有状态组件，将状态集中于单一服务管理。

5. 认为数据库是系统设计最重要的组件，特别强调了合理设计数据表结构和索引的重要性。

文章主张简单实用的设计哲学，反对过度设计和华而不实的复杂架构。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[系统设计的复杂性与适用性]

不同观点：
• [alixanderwang] 认为复杂系统往往缺乏良好的设计，建议在面试中避免过度设计，强调实际需求而非复杂性。
• [motorest] 对“避免多个服务直接写入同一数据库表”的建议提出质疑，认为分布式系统的设计需要权衡数据库接口的便利性与自定义接口的复杂性。
• [bambax] 强调数据库查询的效率，推荐使用视图和存储过程，避免在应用代码中进行连接操作。
• [KronisLV] 批评过度灵活的模式设计（如EAV或JSON列），认为清晰的表结构更易于理解和维护。
• [alphazard] 指出系统设计的核心在于用户接口，而非技术实现，认为接口设计是最关键且难以更改的部分。
• [msiyer] 认为如果多个服务需要写入同一表，可能是服务逻辑重叠的信号，建议重构服务而非增加协调逻辑。
• [lutzh] 强调系统设计应根据具体需求，而非抽象的好坏标准，认为“适合目的”才是关键。
• [tetha] 区分有状态和无状态应用的重要性，指出数据库等持久化存储需要更多经验和谨慎处理。

补充讨论：
• [nvarj] 和 [UncleFullstack] 提到工程师常因追求复杂性而忽视简单解决方案（KISS原则），并举例说明过度设计的实际案例。
• [ZYbCRq22HbJ2y7] 对“使用时间戳代替布尔值”的模式提出质疑，认为并非所有场景都适用。
• [thisbeensaid] 推荐使用DBOS等工具简化系统设计，减少对额外服务的依赖。
• [com] 和 [bravesoul2] 分别提到日志、度量和团队拓扑在系统设计中的重要性。
• [usernamed7] 补充强调系统设计应优化变更，使其易于理解和修改。

争议焦点：
• 多个服务直接访问同一数据库表的利弊（[motorest] vs. [msiyer]）。
• 模式设计的灵活性（[KronisLV] vs. 可能的EAV支持者）。
• 系统设计的核心是技术实现还是用户接口（[alphazard] vs. 其他技术导向观点）。

44921137.article_content:
I see a lot of bad system design advice. One classic is the LinkedIn-optimized “bet you never heard of
queues
” style of post, presumably aimed at people who are new to the industry. Another is the Twitter-optimized “you’re a terrible engineer if you ever store booleans in a database” clever trick
1
. Even good system design advice can be kind of bad. I love
Designing Data-Intensive Applications
, but I don’t think it’s particularly useful for most system design problems engineers will run into.
What is system design? In my view, if software design is how you assemble lines of code, system design is how you assemble
services
. The primitives of software design are variables, functions, classes, and so on. The primitives of system design are app servers, databases, caches, queues, event buses, proxies, and so on.
This post is my attempt to write down, in broad strokes, everything I know about good system design. A lot of the concrete judgment calls do come down to experience, which I can’t convey in this post. But I’m trying to write down what I can.
Recognizing good design
What does good system design look like? I’ve written before that it
looks underwhelming
. In practice, it looks like nothing going wrong for a long time. You can tell that you’re in the presence of good design if you have thoughts like “huh, this ended up being easier than I expected”, or “I never have to think about this part of the system, it’s fine”. Paradoxically, good design is self-effacing: bad design is often more impressive than good. I’m always suspicious of impressive-looking systems. If a system has distributed-consensus mechanisms, many different forms of event-driven communication, CQRS, and other clever tricks, I wonder if there’s some fundamental bad decision that’s being compensated for (or if the system is just straightforwardly over-designed).
I’m often alone on this. Engineers look at complex systems with many interesting parts and think “wow, a lot of system design is happening here!” In fact, a complex system usually reflects an absence of good design. I say “usually” because sometimes you do need complex systems. I’ve worked on many systems that earned their complexity. However, a complex system that works always evolves from a simple system that works. Beginning from scratch with a complex system is a really bad idea.
State and statelessness
The hard part about software design is state. If you’re storing any kind of information for any amount of time, you have a lot of tricky decisions to make about how you save, store and serve it. If you’re not storing information
2
, your app is “stateless”. As a non-trivial example, GitHub has an internal API that takes a PDF file and returns a HTML rendering of it. That’s a real stateless service. Anything that writes to a database is stateful.
You should try and minimize the amount of stateful components in any system. (In a sense this is trivially true, because you should try to minimize the amount of
all
components in a system, but stateful components are particularly dangerous.) The reason you should do this is that
stateful components can get into a bad state
. Our stateless PDF-rendering service will safely run forever, as long as you’re doing broadly sensible things: e.g. running it in a restartable container so that if anything goes wrong it can be automatically killed and restored to working order. A stateful service can’t be automatically repaired like this. If your database gets a bad entry in it (for instance, an entry with a format that triggers a crash in your application), you have to manually go in and fix it up. If your database runs out of room, you have to figure out some way to prune unneeded data or expand it.
What this means in practice is having one service that knows about the state - i.e. it talks to a database - and other services that do stateless things. Avoid having five different services all write to the same table. Instead, have four of them send API requests (or emit events) to the first service, and keep the writing logic in that one service. If you can, it’s worth doing this for the read logic as well, although I’m less absolutist about this. It’s
sometimes
better for services to do a quick read of the
user_sessions
table than to make a 2x slower HTTP request to an internal sessions service.
Databases
Since managing state is the most important part of system design, the most important component is usually where that state lives: the database. I’ve spent most of my time working with SQL databases (MySQL and PostgreSQL), so that’s what I’m going to talk about.
Schemas and indexes
If you need to store something in a database, the first thing to do is define a table with the schema you need. Schema design should be flexible, because once you have thousands or millions of records, it can be an enormous pain to change the schema. However, if you make it too flexible (e.g. by sticking everything in a “value” JSON column, or using “keys” and “values”

主要讨论点：[系统设计的复杂性与适用性]

不同观点：
• [alixanderwang] 认为复杂系统往往缺乏良好的设计，建议在面试中避免过度设计，强调实际需求而非复杂性。
• [motorest] 对“避免多个服务直接写入同一数据库表”的建议提出质疑，认为分布式系统的设计需要权衡数据库接口的便利性与自定义接口的复杂性。
• [bambax] 强调数据库查询的效率，推荐使用视图和存储过程，避免在应用代码中进行连接操作。
• [KronisLV] 批评过度灵活的模式设计（如EAV或JSON列），认为清晰的表结构更易于理解和维护。
• [alphazard] 指出系统设计的核心在于用户接口，而非技术实现，认为接口设计是最关键且难以更改的部分。
• [msiyer] 认为如果多个服务需要写入同一表，可能是服务逻辑重叠的信号，建议重构服务而非增加协调逻辑。
• [lutzh] 强调系统设计应根据具体需求，而非抽象的好坏标准，认为“适合目的”才是关键。
• [tetha] 区分有状态和无状态应用的重要性，指出数据库等持久化存储需要更多经验和谨慎处理。

补充讨论：
• [nvarj] 和 [UncleFullstack] 提到工程师常因追求复杂性而忽视简单解决方案（KISS原则），并举例说明过度设计的实际案例。
• [ZYbCRq22HbJ2y7] 对“使用时间戳代替布尔值”的模式提出质疑，认为并非所有场景都适用。
• [thisbeensaid] 推荐使用DBOS等工具简化系统设计，减少对额外服务的依赖。
• [com] 和 [bravesoul2] 分别提到日志、度量和团队拓扑在系统设计中的重要性。
• [usernamed7] 补充强调系统设计应优化变更，使其易于理解和修改。

争议焦点：
• 多个服务直接访问同一数据库表的利弊（[motorest] vs. [msiyer]）。
• 模式设计的灵活性（[KronisLV] vs. 可能的EAV支持者）。
• 系统设计的核心是技术实现还是用户接口（[alphazard] vs. 其他技术导向观点）。
